{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the belly line (stroke 3), the lower half of the fish body, and it reached the tail junction around the 5-minute mark. That was the last body piece to arrive, so the full outline could light up. I was behind the top line for the first few minutes, which put pressure on the tail work. Near the end I added a bridge into the upper fin. Hana confirmed the fin was lit afterwards, but Sofia and Hana were also working that joint, so I can't say how much of the fix was mine. The final picture still showed a few pale bits near the junction: a stray line and a small arc in the notch. We judged them harmless to the outline, but I haven't seen the fallen result, so I can't promise the judge reads it as a fish.

Execution: I stuck with one stroke and finished it rather than splitting it with Sofia, which avoided doubling up. Looking back, I started slowly and should have taken Sofia's offer of help on the last stretch sooner. I also kept the status updates accurate. Once the fish was lit, I stayed off the junction as agreed and didn't add dominoes that could jam it.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed about where the belly was, pointed at the spots I meant, and told people when I was moving to the tail. I redirected Sofia to the upper fin when I didn't need her on the belly. Between 7:30 and 9:45 I sent several cheerful 'hands off' messages that mostly repeated what others had said, so that was more noise than content.

Leadership: Sofia and Hana set the plan and the roles, and I followed them rather than leading. My contribution was keeping the mood light and the group calm during the final countdown. I didn't drive any decisions, and I'd want to take more initiative next time, for example by proposing an earlier full-table check of the junction."}
